newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt spokesman says not expecting poll soon.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt spokesman says not expecting poll soon.

text.p: Japan's chief government spokesman said on Thursday that he does not expect Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to call a general election anytime soon.
"There is nothing but (the issue of) Okinawa on Prime Minister Hashimoto's mind," chief cabinet secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a regular news conference.
"I understand that the conditions have not reached that stage (in which he can call an election)," he said.
Japanese media reports earlier this week said Hashimoto was expected to hold elections on October 20.
Kajiyama said Hashimoto will concentrate on resolving the issue of the concentration of U.S. military bases on the southern island prefecture of Okinawa.

Earlier, an official with Japan's ruling coalition said Hashimoto, who is also president of the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), was planning to meet the leaders of the other two coalition parties at 1 p.m. (0400 GMT) today.
Hashimoto, the leaders of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Sakigake party, are widely expected to discuss the timing of long-anticipated general elections.

On Wednesday, SDP head Tomiichi Murayama and Sakigake's Shoichi Ide had expressed anger at a flurry of newspaper reports attributed to LDP sources which said a general election was likely to be held on October 20.
